bullets.title: NVDA: CEO dismisses chip delay, Japan AI factory with 27,500 Vera Rubin GPUs live; AAPL overtakes as most valuable
bullets.body: Jensen Huang pushed back hard on 'chip delay' narrative, saying 'giant amounts' of Vera Rubin GPUs are coming and Japan's first AI factory (27,500 units) is operational. Separately, AAPL briefly surpassed NVDA as world's most valuable company at $4.92T vs NVDA's $4.86T amid the sector selloff.

bullets.title: Kimi K3 / China AI triggers record momentum selloff; semis near bear market (-20%)
bullets.body: MS TMT Momentum is down -40% in 17 days, the fastest/deepest selloff on record (vs -29% in early 2021). China's Moonshot Kimi K3 (2.8T-parameter open-weight MoE) rekindled DeepSeek fears, sending AMD -4.1%, MU -3.4%, CDNS -6.9%, ALAB -5.2%, and CRDO -5.7% in pre-market; SOX approaching -20% bear market threshold. Jefferies notes K3 API pricing jumped 223% vs prior version, which JPM argues makes it uncompetitive on cost-per-task vs Grok 4.5/Claude 4.8.

bullets.title: CDNS/SNPS: Mizuho Buy the dip — Kimi K3 uses EDA tools, doesn't replace them
bullets.body: CDNS and SNPS dropped ~10% after Moonshot's K3 autonomously designed a chip in 48 hours using open-source tools (OpenRoad at 45nm), not proprietary CDNS/SNPS solvers. Mizuho argues agentic AI drives incremental EDA usage, could triple core EDA TAM, and K3's result used academic nodes where CDNS/SNPS have no durable edge—recommending buying the dip.

bullets.title: NFLX: -11% post-earnings; MS cuts PT to $83, Bernstein to $95; 3Q guidance disappoints
bullets.body: Netflix fell ~11.6% after 2Q revenue of $12.6B (+13.5% YoY) was offset by weaker-than-expected UCAN trends and below-consensus 3Q revenue guidance (+11% ex-FX vs +12% prior). Morgan Stanley cut PT to $83 from $90; Bernstein cut to $95 from $100. Citi warns bears see multiple compression toward traditional video media multiples.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini 3.5 Pro delayed ~1 month on coding gaps; stock -4.5% pre-market
bullets.body: GOOGL fell ~4.5% as reports emerged that Gemini 3.5 Pro is delayed roughly one month due to coding capability gaps vs. peers (per Morgan Stanley). GOOGL reports earnings Wednesday after close next week; AMD Advancing AI event also Wednesday-Thursday.

bullets.title: META: Hires AWS Compute Chief Dave Brown, signals enterprise cloud push; expanding Louisiana DC to 5GW
bullets.body: Meta is hiring Dave Brown, one of AWS's most senior executives (nearly two decades at Amazon), to lead its cloud infrastructure buildout as it weighs offering cloud services. Separately, Meta is expanding its Louisiana data center from 2GW to 5GW with a $50B+ commitment, and JPM notes Meta 2026 capex at $125-145B.

bullets.title: NVDA bullish counter-thesis: UBS says open-source AI adoption expands inference demand
bullets.body: UBS argues open-source model adoption (growing from sub-1% to multiples of that by mid-2026) is net positive for NVDA because most open-source models are trained/fine-tuned on NVDA hardware, yielding superior inference performance. The firm views open-source as incremental demand, not cannibalistic—and NVDA's Nemotron family positions it for agentic workflows.

bullets.title: MRVL: Buy maintained, $280 PT; F2Q27E +12% QoQ revenue, margins above Street
bullets.body: An analyst maintains Buy on MRVL with $280 price target, forecasting F2Q27 revenue +12% QoQ with ~59% non-GAAP gross margin vs. Street at 58.8%, and F3Q27E +13% QoQ vs. consensus +11%. QCOM initiated at Hold by same analyst. MS separately sized scale-up networking TAM at $73B and upgraded KEYS to OW, with AVGO, ALAB, and MRVL as copper/ASIC ramp beneficiaries.

bullets.title: PLTR: DA Davidson upgrades to Buy; pullback is attractive entry despite NHS concerns
bullets.body: DA Davidson upgraded PLTR to Buy, arguing high-value products and competitive moat warrant a premium to the 30% growth-camp peer multiple. UK NHS contract concerns dismissed as <1% of revenues. BRZE also flagged as taking share from Salesforce/Adobe, trading at 28x CY26 FCF vs. 39x for 20% growth peers.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: Citi upgrades FOXA to Top Pick ($78 PT); ROKU PT raised to $157 on deal synergies
bullets.body: Citi upgraded FOXA to Top Pick with $78 PT, calling the Roku deal FCF accretive one year after close (vs. two-year guide) with ~$1B annual EBITDA synergies and close by 4Q26. ROKU PT raised to $157 from $120 though Citi maintains Neutral on ROKU. FOXA flagged as strong relative-value play in streaming consolidation.

bullets.title: ALLY: Unusual options volume 1,456% above average ahead of Jul-21 earnings
bullets.body: ALLY showed 35,866 options contracts traded vs. 2,464-contract average (1,456% above avg) with a 0.00 put/call ratio, signaling aggressive bullish positioning ahead of earnings before market open on July 21.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone carrier-lock policy shifts value to VZ/T; Baltra chip delays signal AI roadmap risk
bullets.body: Apple iPhones financed via carrier installment plans are no longer being unlocked, locking customers to carrier networks—positive for AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon but negative for Apple's ecosystem control. Separately, Apple is reportedly hunting external AI chip acquisitions due to delays in its own 'Baltra' server chip program. Mizuho views AAPL as relatively safe 'anti-AI capex' play with raised prices and stable unit volumes.

bullets.title: EQIX: CBO Jon Lin fired after 17-year tenure; negative read on leadership stability
bullets.body: Equinix's Chief Business Officer Jon Lin was separated/fired on July 18 after 17 years overseeing products and global P&L. Wells Fargo also upgraded SBAC to OW at $210 PT (Citi also maintains Buy on SBAC post-17% pullback, forecasting $12.28 FY26 AFFOPS vs. $12.20 consensus).

bullets.title: NBIS: Raises $775M senior secured debt to accelerate GPU cloud buildout
bullets.body: Nebius entered its first senior secured debt facility of ~$775M (SOFR+250bps, maturing Oct 2030), backed by deployed GPU infrastructure and contracted cash flows from an investment-grade customer. Proceeds fund global full-stack AI cloud expansion; facility plus customer cash flows cover >100% of underlying capex.

bullets.title: DKNG: UBS flags Bet365 as growing competitive threat; PA gaming revenues -1.7% YoY
bullets.body: UBS highlights Bet365 expanded into 6 new US states since early 2025, now covering 38.9% of US population (from 25.5%), making it a more meaningful threat than BetMGM or Caesars. Pennsylvania June gaming revenues fell 1.7% YoY to $535M with iGaming down 10.2%, though sports wagering handle rose 17.9%.

bullets.title: Semi sector: VRT, WDC, CRWV at 52-week lows; ORCL -48% YTD
bullets.body: Pre-market data shows VRT down 2.2% at a 52-week low, WDC down 1.5% at 52-week low, and CRWV down 0.4% YTD also at 52-week low. ORCL is down 48.3% YTD at a 52-week low, NFLX at 52-week low down 45.6% YTD. Memory stocks account for ~2/3 of tech selling since the reversal per MS prime brokerage data.

bullets.title: Mizuho: Semi weakness is rotation not fundamentals; buy TXN analog semis into earnings
bullets.body: Mizuho's buy-side tour found no panic selling in semis—weakness attributed to retail/levered ETF unwinding after SOX's 104% rally from March lows. Analog semis (TXN, STM) flagged as best-positioned for upside: TXN can beat Q2 and hit $5.85B Q3 revenue bogey; analog companies raising prices a second time this year with gross margin expansion ahead. Hyperscalers (META, GOOGL, AMZN) flagged as add-on-weakness.

bullets.title: CCL preferred, NCLH cautious; VIK PT raised to $115 on strongest pricing growth
bullets.body: Jefferies upgrades VIK price target to $115 (from $100) on ~12% Y/Y 2H26 pricing growth vs. peers softening (CCL -12%, RCL -5%, NCLH -6%). NCLH faces material pressure with May-July 2027 pricing down ~28% YoY; FY27 EPS cut 15%. CCL benefits from geographic diversification and 4.2% buyback. Ratings: Buy VIK & CCL; Hold RCL & NCLH.

bullets.title: TSLA/GOOGL/INTC earnings next week; AMD Advancing AI event Wednesday-Thursday
bullets.body: Key week ahead: GOOGL and TSLA report Wednesday after close, INTC Thursday after close. AMD hosting Advancing AI event Wed-Thu. VZ, T, CMCSA, CHTR, NOW, TXN, DLR also on calendar. Fed in blackout before July 29 FOMC; markets pricing 24bp of hikes through year-end.

bullets.title: JPM hyperscaler AI capex thesis intact; $1.4T by 2028; K3 seen as bullish for compute
bullets.body: MS estimates $1.4T hyperscaler capex and 4x compute capacity by 2028. JPM notes Kimi K3 requires GB/B300 chips (cannot fit on single NVDA DGX B200), which is actually bullish for the capex cycle. Hyperscalers approaching FCF neutrality in 2026-27 with further acceleration likely funded via equity/debt. JPM and MS hosting joint hyperscaler equity/credit calls next week (GOOGL, AMZN, META, MSFT, ORCL).
